With `globals: true` in the Vitest config, `describe`, `test`, `expect`, `vi` and the hooks exist without an import. A file that relies on that fails with a `ReferenceError` as soon as the setting is off, and nothing in the file says where the names come from.

A file gets one report for all the names it uses.

`--fix` adds the import, or adds the names to the import from `vitest` that's already there. A new import goes below what has to stay first: a `#!` line, comments about the file like `// @ts-nocheck`, `/// <reference>` or a license, directives like `"use strict"`, and a header comment with an empty line after it. It goes above the comments that touch the first statement, which are about that statement.

If the fix adds the names to a `const { .. } = require("vitest")` line of the file, code that runs before that line gets no value for them. So `--fix` only adds them to a line that is at the top of the file, takes its names from the module itself and has no `...rest` and no comment in its `{ }`. At the top means that nothing but directives, `import` statements, type declarations and other plain `require()` lines stands above it, and that the file has no `export` of a value. Another file could call such an export before the line has run or the `import` has its module. For the same reason, `--fix` adds no names to an `import` of a file that has such an `export`. `--fix` also leaves a file alone that assigns to one of the names, because nothing can assign to an `import` or to a `const`. `--fix-dangerously` adds the names in all these cases, and the assignment then fails.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"vitest/prefer-importing-vitest-globals" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 1} */}
```ts
describe("cart", () => {
  test("starts empty", () => {
    expect(cart.items).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";

describe("cart", () => {
  test("starts empty", () => {
    expect(cart.items).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});
```

A name that the file imports from another package, or declares itself, isn't a global:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { expect, test } from "@playwright/test";

test("starts empty", async ({ page }) => {
  await expect(page.getByRole("listitem")).toHaveCount(0);
});
```

## When not to use it

Turn it off for files that use the globals of another test runner with the same names.
